lead.headline: Amazon tells its engineers to stop tokenmaxxing: token counts and lines of code are "deeply flawed" metrics
lead.summary: Amazon published its revised role guideline for software engineers and managers on Tuesday, a memo first circulated internally in September. It says token usage, AI-tool adoption and code-change counts are deeply flawed when used as targets, because they drive up cost (tokenmaxxing is at odds with frugality) and complexity. They still correlate with real output, so use them "with care and judgment", watching the 10th and 90th percentile teams. AWS VP Marc Brooker told CNBC Amazon looks at feature velocity instead: launches and successful production changes. Amazon has not capped token use, but shut down an internal AI leaderboard in May after people gamed it. The best line for anyone: "If your work does not benefit from current AI tooling, that is a finding, not a failing."

news.headline: Genie 4: DeepMind's world model now does sound, dialogue and live edits
news.summary: Genie 4 adds native audio (ambient sound, music and dialogue) and lets you steer a running world in plain language, with Gemini 3.8 Flash guiding the agent. Scenes stay coherent for about two minutes, roughly double Genie 3, though drift is still a limit. Trusted testers first, then Google AI Ultra and Gemini API partners.

news.headline: Warp breached through a vendor; AI agent traces and telemetry exposed
news.summary: Attackers got in through a third-party vendor and reached agent traces and user telemetry. Warp says it caught it within hours and puts the upper bound at about 1% of users; CrowdStrike and law enforcement are involved. It's still unclear whether code, prompts or credentials were in what leaked.

news.headline: Pages, Keynote and Numbers get AI assistants and MCP on macOS 27
news.summary: Apple's Creator Studio update adds beta assistants, built on Apple and OpenAI models, that design slides in Keynote, draft text in Pages and suggest charts in Numbers. The bigger deal for builders: on macOS 27 the apps get MCP support, so outside agents can read, edit and act inside documents. US English first, arriving in November.

news.headline: Qt Group launches Clate, an AI-native UI design tool for embedded devices
news.summary: Designers prompt in natural language, connect tools over MCP, watch live FPS and memory use, and get production-ready QML for resource-limited hardware. Clate starts as a beta now; the rest of the planned features arrive in early 2027.

x_posts.name: DHH
x_posts.text: Windows Copilot was so terrible it might very well have seeded the AI opposition we now see among normies. Useless functionality, hyped to the moon, and a dumb key on every keyboard that did nothing worthwhile.
x_posts.why: A blunt take on how bad AI products shape public mood.

writers_corner.title: AI SRE: what is it, how could it change on-call – and does it work?
writers_corner.take: Agents doubled how often teams ship, so pages are up too. AI SREs mostly speed up incident investigation in Slack; fully autonomous fixes are still stage demos.
writers_corner.quote: Almost all tech companies have seen their PR frequency double in a year due to AI agents.
writers_corner.read_note: free intro, rest for paid subscribers

quick_hit.label: Quick hit
quick_hit.text: Anthropic's Frontier Red Team details five attack chains in browsers and operating systems, found with an unreleased internal model, that led to remote code execution and other critical impacts with little to no user interaction. All were reported to vendors, who get 90 days to patch.
